name: Abel
charge: Bringing the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof
summary: Abel brought the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof, and the Lord had respect unto him and his offering. Hebrews witnesses to his faith, and Christ names him righteous Abel. His brother slew him, but his blood cried from the ground and his faith remained a testimony.
offense: Abel brought the firstlings of his flock and the fat thereof, and the Lord had respect unto Abel and his offering (Genesis 4:4). His gift was not described merely by its presence at the altar: the firstlings and the fat are specifically named. The later commands concerning the firstborn and the Lord's portion of the fat give precepts for the honour shown in that offering (Exodus 13:12; Leviticus 3:16). Hebrews supplies the decisive testimony: by faith Abel offered a more excellent sacrifice than Cain and obtained witness that he was righteous (Hebrews 11:4). His obedience cannot be reduced to the material of the gift while forgetting the man who brought it. John likewise distinguishes the brothers by their works: Cain's were evil and Abel's righteous (1 John 3:12). Worship and conduct belonged to the same account before God.
judgment: God testified of Abel's gifts, and Christ named him righteous Abel (Hebrews 11:4; Matthew 23:35). His brother's violence did not reverse that judgment. The man rejected by Cain was accepted by God, and the blood shed in the field was not beyond God's hearing (Genesis 4:8-10). Being dead, he yet speaks. Hebrews preserves his faith as a witness after his life was taken; Genesis preserves the cry of his blood. The blessing was a righteous standing before God, not immunity from the wickedness of another. His case condemns envy without making the victim's death evidence against his obedience. Christ places Abel at the beginning of the blood of the prophets shed from the foundation of the world (Luke 11:49-51). His witness therefore reaches beyond the offering itself: righteous works drew his brother's hatred, and the murder of the righteous became a pattern repeated against God's messengers (1 John 3:12). Cain silenced his brother's voice in the field, but could not silence the testimony God gave of him.

verses.text: And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.
And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.
And Abel, he also brought of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:
But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.
By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
That thou shalt set apart unto the Lord all that openeth the matrix, and every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast; the males shall be the Lord’s.
And the priest shall burn them upon the altar: it is the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour: all the fat is the Lord’s.
Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

text.text: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute:
That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation;
From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation.

entries.commentary: Here is the birth of trade and of religion with Cain and Abel: Abel a keeper of sheep, Cain a tiller of the ground.

The Most High had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and Cain was wroth. Remember the earth was cursed in chapter 3, so it was hard to get fruit out of the ground; that is part of why Cain was angry.

The Most High is calling Cain to repent. Cain knew that the Most High required animal sacrifice, because the sacrificial law was ordained at [Genesis 3:21](/bible/genesis/3#v21). If Cain would not repent, sin lay at the door; he would become subject to Satan and Satan would rule over him.
When Cain talked with Abel, Abel was trying to get Cain to repent. Abel was a prophet.
Cain was cursed from the earth and made a fugitive and a vagabond, the same low estate spoken of the serpent in chapter 3.

Every one that findeth me shall slay me is proof in the pudding, like we brought out in [Genesis 1](/bible/genesis/1), that there were more people on the earth than Adam's household. The mark set upon Cain changed him; at the beginning Cain looked like everybody else, and the Most High marked him so that any finding him would not kill him.

Cain found his wife in the land of Nod; there were already people on the earth during the time of Adam. Cain built a city, and you do not build a city for three people; this is more proof that the earth was peopled. The lands in those days were named after men, which is why the land was called Nod. Cain called the city after the name of his son, as the wicked call their lands after their own names.

This is the first time you read about a man taking multiple wives, and it is the sons of the wicked who did it. In the beginning it was one wife. When you read about the sons of God in [Genesis 5](/bible/genesis/5) you do not read about them taking multiple wives; only the sons of the wicked.
An instructor of every artificer in brass and iron: these men started making weapons. This is the first you read about weapons being created.

Lamech was murdering men; Satan was working with the sons of the wicked. Lamech knew the commandment thou shalt not kill was in force in his day; that is why he appealed to Cain's sevenfold, saying seventy and sevenfold. They knew the commandments during that time.

Seth was appointed another seed instead of Abel. Through Seth men began to call upon the name of the Lord; they started to worship the Most High and keep the commandments, while the line of Cain went on in evil and wickedness. That is why the Most High chose the line of Seth. --- Topics: [Clean and Unclean Meats](/encyclopedia/clean-and-unclean-meats) · [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' seat. Whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works, for they say, and do not. They bind heavy burdens and lay them on men's shoulders, but will not move them with one of their fingers.

All their works they do for to be seen of men. They love the uppermost rooms at feasts and the chief seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the markets. He that is greatest among you shall be your servant. Whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased, and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.

Woe unto you: ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in. They devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer, and shall receive the greater damnation. There is a lesson in what they would not do. Where leadership provokes a man to works and he finds himself falling behind, he should take it to heart, because telling people who they are without putting in the labour yields no fruit.

They compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Their rules about swearing by the gold rather than the temple, and by the gift rather than the altar, are called out as blindness: the temple sanctifies the gold and the altar sanctifies the gift.

They pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin and have omitted the weightier matters of the law: judgment, mercy, and faith. These ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.

They make clean the outside of the cup and platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Cleanse first that which is within. They are likened unto whited sepulchres, beautiful outward but within full of dead men's bones. Outwardly they appear righteous unto men, but within are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.

They build the tombs of the prophets and say they would not have shed their blood, and by saying it they witness against themselves that they are the children of them which killed the prophets. Upon them comes all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias. This is the plainest speaking in the gospel. Christ was no soft man with these teachers of the law who did not believe it.
O Jerusalem, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not. Behold, your house is left unto you desolate.
Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of beast: it is mine. The firstborn belong to the Most High.

Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place, and no leavened bread is eaten. This day came ye out in the month Abib: the first month of the year, falling at the first new moon of the spring.

When the Lord brings Israel into the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, a land flowing with milk and honey, this service is kept in this month: seven days of unleavened bread, and in the seventh day a feast to the Lord, with no leaven seen in all thy quarters. Thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt. It is a sign upon thine hand and a memorial between thine eyes, that the Lord's law may be in thy mouth. Thou shalt therefore keep this ordinance in his season from year to year: the Passover is kept every year.

All that openeth the matrix is set apart unto the Lord; the matrix is the womb. Every firstling that cometh of a beast which thou hast, the males are the Lord's. Every firstling of an ass is redeemed with a lamb, and if not redeemed its neck is broken; and all the firstborn of man among thy children shalt thou redeem.

When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, What is this? thou shalt say, By strength of hand the Lord brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage: when Pharaoh would hardly let us go, the Lord slew all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, therefore the firstborn are sacrificed or redeemed. The children must be taught the righteousness of why the feast is kept. Ask the children of this land why they keep Christmas and they answer that Santa Claus is coming down the chimney; Israel's children are to be taught the works of the Most High instead. It is for a token upon thine hand and for frontlets between thine eyes, for by strength of hand the Lord brought us forth out of Egypt.

When Pharaoh let the people go, God led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near, lest peradventure the people repent when they see war and return to Egypt. Israel would have been fearful at the sight of the Philistine army and turned back. The people felt a false security in Egypt: in the wilderness they murmured for the fish, the leeks, the onions, and the garlick of Egypt and loathed the light bread; and when the Assyrians came, Israel again ran down to Egypt for help. The same spirit holds the people in America today: a little job, government assistance, a car, food from the store, and they never want this kingdom to come down. But the Most High has something much greater in store: the world, the earth, and many mansions. So God led the people about, through the way of the wilderness of the Red Sea, and the children of Israel went up harnessed out of the land of Egypt.
Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for Joseph had straitly sworn the children of Israel, saying, God will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

They took their journey from Succoth and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness. The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, to go by day and night. He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood) · [The Sabbath](/encyclopedia/the-sabbath)

The peace offering of the herd, whether male or female, must be offered without blemish before the Lord: no bruise, no cut, no stain, nothing superfluous like an extra member. Whatever the sacrifice is for the Lord, it has to be the best of the best, a flawless sacrifice. The Passover lamb shows how that was carried out. The lamb was without blemish, a male of the first year, taken out from the sheep and kept from the goats, because if it got in a fight it would take a blemish, a bruise, a cut. It was kept up to the fourteenth day, isolated and given nothing but water, so that it purified itself; and it was eaten roast with fire, not raw and not sodden with water, with the purtenance thereof, for after those days there was nothing left within it.

The peace offering could be of the herd or of the flock, a lamb or a goat, male or female without blemish, unlike the burnt offering of chapter 1, which was a male. The offerer laid his hand upon the head of his offering and killed it at the door of the tabernacle, and Aaron's sons sprinkled the blood upon the altar round about. The blood, the fat that covers the inwards, the two kidneys with the fat upon them by the flanks, and the caul above the liver were the Lord's, burned upon the altar, the food of the offering made by fire for a sweet savour; the breast and the right shoulder were for the priest. All the fat is the Lord's.

It shall be a perpetual statute that ye eat neither fat nor blood. This is a controversial scripture: brothers and sisters ask whether we are cut off for eating fat. Having that question is a good thing; it means you are reading to understand, not reading just to say you read four chapters. [Leviticus 7](/bible/leviticus/7) answers it in context: whosoever eateth the fat of the beast of which men offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord shall be cut off. This is the law of sacrifice, which we are no longer under; Christ is the end of the law for righteousness. The sacrifices stopped after 70 AD at the fall of Jerusalem, when there was no longer a temple. And there is no way to take off all the fat of the meat you eat; we are not koshering our meat.
